card.name: Start of a drug or brand name
card.fires_on: The first piece of a capitalized drug or brand name that is split into parts, such as U in Ustekinumab, VI in VIJOICE, or Ab in Abatacept. It also fires on a few capitalized label words such as Cent and Ad.

modes.label: Split drug name start
modes.description: The opening piece of a drug or brand name after words like of, with, or a comma.
modes.example: Initial Intravenous Dosage of<< U>>stekinumab in Adult Patients

modes.label: Brand name VIJOICE
modes.description: VI at the start of the brand name VIJOICE after treated with.

modes.label: Other label words
modes.description: The first piece of a label term, such as an FDA system name, or the word patient before labeling.
modes.example: based on reports in FDA’s<< Ad>>verse Events Reporting System (AERS)

card.writes: It mostly promotes odd non-English tokens and suppresses ph- pieces, so there is no clear link to the next word.
card.plain: It fires on the first letters of a drug name that gets broken into pieces, right before the rest of the name.
